messages.subject: Detection history function error
parts:
Hi Juergen (and anyone else willing to help),

 

My name is Angie, I’m a student in the Research Experience for Undergraduates (REU) program at the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory in Colorado, USA. I’m currently conducting research using wildlife camera traps and I’ve been trying to use the camtrapR and unmarked programs in R Studio for part of my data analysis. I’m having an issue with the detectionHistory command function within camtrapR. It keeps saying: “Error in if (occasionLength > ncol(camOp)/2) stop("occasionLength may not be greater than half the total number of days in camOp") : argument is of length zero”. I’ve tried changing the camOp data by adding in more days, I’ve tried various numbers as the occasionLength, I’ve copied exactly from the example given in the help section. Nothing has worked, it keeps showing this error message. I assume the issue is with the format of the data in camOp, but I’ve copied the exact format as the example sample data given in the program, and I’m still having this issue.


I've attached the following data:

1. "metadata2.csv" = (recordTableSample) data

2. "CTtablesample2.csv" = (camtraps) data

3. "camOp3.csv" = (camOperation) data


**When they attach here, the date format changes to MM/DD/YY, but when loaded into R the csv files always show the dates formatted as YYYY-MM-DD, not sure why it's messing up here.

 


Here is a summary of the code I've used:


> recordtable.dat<-read.csv("metadata2.csv")

> CTtable.dat<-read.csv("CTtablesample2.csv")

> cameraOperation(CTtable = CTtable.dat, stationCol = "Station", setupCol = "Setup_date", retrievalCol = "Retrieval_date", hasProblems = FALSE, dateFormat = "%Y-%m-%d", writecsv = TRUE)

> camOp3.dat<-read.csv("camOp3.csv")

> detectionHistory(recordTable = recordtable.dat, species = "human", camOp = "camOp3.dat", output = c("binary"), stationCol = "Station", speciesCol = "Species", recordDateTimeCol = "DateTimeOriginal", recordDateTimeFormat = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", occasionLength = 1, day1 = "2019-06-02", includeEffort = TRUE, scaleEffort = TRUE, datesAsOccasionNames = TRUE, writecsv = TRUE)   



This is the error I keep receiving:


"Error in if (occasionLength > ncol(camOp)/2) stop("occasionLength may not be greater than half the total number of days in camOp") : 

  argument is of length zero"


           

If you have any idea what I’m doing wrong or how I can fix this issue, I would greatly appreciate any help!! 

 

Thank you for your time and consideration,

 

Angie

Angie

messages.subject: Re: Detection history function error
parts:
***UPDATE***

Philip Faure contacted me with the solution to this issue!! To summarize, the formatting of the data tables had to be specifically characterized through R because it was reading the data table columns incorrectly. I've attached the updated sample code script (created and provided by Philip Faure) that worked for me.

Thanks again to Philip!!!

Angie
